objects.language: English Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard (TREFS) governs how a sufficiently recognized real-world, economic, operational, transactional, digital, autonomous, machine-generated, or value-affecting occurrence is transformed into a coherent governed event structure capable of progressing through the subsequent stages of the TREGA™ lifecycle. TREFS establishes the governance conditions through which recognized occurrence elements are structurally organized into an Event Formation, including the identification of materially relevant formation components, their assembly, material formation dependencies, operational root association, and the integrity of the resulting formation.

English Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard (TREBS) governs how a sufficiently formed real-world, economic, operational, transactional, digital, autonomous, machine-generated, or value-affecting event is bounded as a distinct governed event by establishing what belongs within its governed extent, what remains outside it, where separation from adjacent or overlapping activity is required, and when an established Event Boundary must be reconsidered or revised. TREBS receives a Governed Formed Event from the Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard (TREFS) and establishes the governed boundary necessary for that event to proceed through subsequent TREGA™ lifecycle stages without allowing Event Boundary governance to determine Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, Event-to-Value Association, Event Relationships, legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, tax liability, or jurisdiction-specific tax consequences.

English ------------------------------ Canonical Definition The Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard (TRETS) governs how a sufficiently bounded real-world, economic, operational, transactional, digital, autonomous, machine-generated, or value-affecting event is temporally situated through governed identification of its operational time, start, completion, duration, and temporal order. TRETS establishes the governance conditions through which a Governed Bounded Event becomes a Governed Temporally Situated Event capable of progressing through subsequent TREGA™ lifecycle stages. It governs the temporal representation of what happened operationally without determining the legal tax point, tax period, filing period, recognition date under tax law, legal timing of tax liability, or any other jurisdiction-specific taxation consequence.

UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard (TREPS) governs how human, organizational, digital, machine, autonomous, infrastructural, and other materially relevant actors are represented as participants in a spatially and temporally governed Tax-Relevant Event. TREPS establishes the governance conditions under which an actor may legitimately be associated with the event, distinguished from other actors, represented according to its operational participation, and maintained as part of the governed event representation. TREPS governs participation in the event. It does not determine whether a participant is legally a taxpayer, taxable person, liable party, beneficial owner, permanent establishment, tax representative, withholding agent, employer, employee, supplier, customer, or any other jurisdiction-specific legal or tax status.

UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard (TRVAS) governs how value references, value states, value changes, and other governed value results are associated with a Governed Participatory Event so that the event can carry a sufficiently structured representation of value into subsequent Tax-Relevant Event governance. TRVAS establishes which governed value information legitimately belongs to the event, how that relationship is represented, how multiple value associations are distinguished, how value states and changes are connected to the event, and how those associations remain traceable. TRVAS does not determine the origin, emergence, development, degradation, nullification, restoration, extinction, ownership, economic meaning, or complete lifecycle of value. Those questions belong to VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism and other appropriate governance architectures. TRVAS also does not determine taxable value, Tax Base, consideration under law, customs value, transfer-pricing value, market value under a jurisdiction-specific rule, deductible amount, taxable income, taxable gain, tax rate, or Tax Liability.

objects.canonicalDefinition: Value Identification Standard (VIS) is the first Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture and governs the methodological conditions under which a potential or existing manifestation of value can be identified, distinguished, bounded, described, and established as a governable Value Object within the value lifecycle.
objects.coreQuestion: What value is being governed, and how can it be sufficiently identified and bounded before its origin, existence, state, and lifecycle are determined?

objects.canonicalDefinition: Value Origin Standard (VOS) is the second Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism and governs the identification, definition, relationship, conditions, and documentation of the origin from which governed value can emerge.

Value Emergence Standard (VES) is the third Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture and governs the conditions under which potential value arising from an identified value origin becomes existent value within a defined Value Context.

Value Recognition Standard (VRS) is the fourth Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture governing the conditions under which existing value may be formally recognized as value within a defined governance context.
objects.coreQuestion: When can existing value be recognized as value within its defined governance context?

objects.canonicalDefinition: Value State Standard (VSS) is the fifth Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture governing the identification, classification, determination, transition readiness, and persistent representation of the current governed state of value.
objects.coreQuestion: What is the current governed state of value?

objects.canonicalDefinition: Value Change Standard (VCS) is the Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture that governs the identification, characterization, magnitude determination, causation linkage, and recording of material change affecting existing governed value.
objects.coreQuestion: When has existing value materially changed, and what change has occurred to it?

objects.canonicalDefinition: Value Development Standard (VDS) is the Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture that governs how existing value develops positively over time through identifiable growth, maturation, compounding, strengthening, capability expansion, productive improvement, or other forms of governed positive development.
objects.coreQuestion: How does existing value increase, strengthen, mature, compound, or otherwise develop over time?

objects.canonicalDefinition: Value Degradation Standard (VDGS) is the Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture that governs how existing positive value weakens, declines, deteriorates, erodes, loses capability, loses utility, becomes impaired, or otherwise undergoes progressive negative development while value continues to exist.
objects.coreQuestion: How does existing value weaken, decline, deteriorate, or become progressively impaired while value still exists?

objects.canonicalDefinition: Value Nullification Standard (VNS) is the Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture that governs the conditions, thresholds, mechanisms, determinations, and governed transitions through which previously existing positive value reaches a legitimate zero-value condition.
objects.coreQuestion: When and through what governed transition does existing positive value reach a zero-value condition?

objects.canonicalDefinition: Value Restoration Standard (VRSS) is the tenth Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture governing how previously existing value that has become degraded, impaired, lost, dormant, inaccessible, or zero may legitimately re-emerge as governed value.

Value Extinction Standard (VXSS) is the Parent Standard within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture that governs the terminal lifecycle condition in which previously existing value ceases to exist as recoverable value within the governed lifecycle.
objects.coreQuestion: When does value cease to exist as recoverable value within the governed lifecycle?
